intro: Libya is a large desert country on the Mediterranean, with some of the best Roman and Greek ruins in the world. Since 2011 it has been divided by conflict.

chapters.title: Greeks, Phoenicians and Romans
text: Greeks founded Cyrene in the east around 630 BC, and Phoenicians built trading towns in the west. Under Rome, Leptis Magna became a grand city, birthplace of Emperor Septimius Severus.
Garamantes in the Fezzan built underground water channels to farm the Sahara.

chapters.title: Islam, Ottomans and Italy
text: Arabs brought Islam in the 640s. The Ottomans ruled from 1551. Italy invaded in 1911, and Omar Mukhtar led resistance until he was executed in 1931; he is a national hero.
Libya was a battlefield in World War Two.

chapters.title: Kingdom, Gaddafi and division
text: Libya became independent in 1951 as a kingdom. Oil was found in 1959. In 1969 Muammar Gaddafi seized power and ruled for 42 years.
In 2011 an uprising, backed by NATO air strikes, overthrew Gaddafi. Since then rival governments in the west and east have competed for power.

keyTerms.meaning: Two groups each claiming to rule the country.
